source_weighting_policy.applies_to: Hermes/taskpool lane=work tasks, including project aliases hermes and hermes-agent.
source_weighting_policy.preflight: Load project profile, repo AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md when a repo is touched, and relevant Workpad/handoff context before planning or implementation.

weights.rule: Highest authority for current taskpool health and closeout gates.

weights.source: task note mission envelope and acceptance evidence
weights.rule: Defines the specific task boundary and completion criteria.
Authoritative for implementation feasibility and regression proof.
Reference only until mapped to Hermes primitives with reproducible evidence.

source_weighting_policy.conflict_rule: When runtime gates, task note, external claims, or repo evidence disagree, record the conflict and keep lifecycle advancement fail-closed unless current runtime evidence resolves it.

conventions: Markdown task notes are canonical; dashboards are derived
Fail closed on missing evidence, stale claims, invalid lifecycle transitions, or missing project profile
Do not execute Markdown task bodies as scripts
Scoped local commits only; do not push unless explicitly requested
acceptance: p10-health remains Grade A or any degradation is explicitly classified
forbidden: Starting a worker without project profile context
Marking task done without structured evidence
Treating model agreement as evidence without claim-linked artifacts

lark_task_execution_policy.primary_goal: Improve Hermes/local-brain control-plane behavior with bounded, evidence-backed changes rather than open-ended advisory notes.
execution_order: reproduce the issue or gather baseline evidence
land the smallest scoped code/config/skill change
run focused regression plus Hermes selfcheck/P10 where applicable
lark_task_execution_policy.closeout_rule: A task is complete only with structured implementation evidence, focused verification output, and no unresolved high-severity selfcheck failure.

backend_contract_policy.contract_scope: Hermes CLI, gateway, cron, taskpool, diagnostics, and profile/runtime state boundaries
backend_contract_policy.schema_rule: Runtime data migrations must be backward compatible and tolerate historical malformed rows without global scheduler/taskpool failure.
backend_contract_policy.compatibility_rule: Prefer no-agent deterministic watchdogs for health/maintenance jobs; avoid provider-dependent summaries for routine control-plane checks.

required_checks: focused Python tests or py_compile for touched scripts
regression_coverage_policy.rollback_rule: If a Hermes runtime patch introduces scheduler/taskpool regression, revert the patch and preserve the failing state as evidence.
